boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Hartville record (January 9-11, 1863) in Marmaduke's First Expedition into Missouri [January 1863]. The frozen interval includes Porter's capture of the Hartville garrison on January 9 and the engagement of January 11; the Marshfield and Sand Spring burnings and the retreat to Batesville are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Detachment of infantry, cavalry, and artillery (approx. 700) [US], and the frozen US bound is 700; the live field reads 700 (US 700; CS 0). Britton says Merrill's column numbered about eight hundred, joined at Hartville by one hundred and eighty cavalry, that prisoners put the Confederates at five thousand, that eight hundred Federal muskets fired the first volley, and that Dunlap was left with his regiment of two hundred and fifty men. Marmaduke's January 18 dispatch gives the enemy as 1,500 infantry and 500 cavalry and Porter's column as 600; his February 1 report gives 2,500 Federal troops and Porter about 700 effective men.
claims.rationale: March strengths, a prisoners' estimate and interested enemy estimates at different times. The frozen 700 has no inspected basis. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live CS zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Confederate victory and the live result Confederate Victory. Marmaduke says the enemy gave way and retreated in disorder, leaving dead, wounded and arms. Britton says most of Merrill's command retired on the Lebanon road, but Dunlap's regiment held its position until the Confederates retreated before sunset, leaving their dead and severely wounded. NPS says the Confederates compelled the Union to retreat but abandoned the raid.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The accounts conflict on which side left the field.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 407 total (US 78; CS 329), as does the live field. Britton gives the Federal loss as 7 killed, 64 wounded, 5 prisoners and 2 missing, and Marmaduke's reported loss as 12 killed, 96 wounded and 3 missing. Marmaduke's January 18 dispatch gives 15 killed and 70 wounded, including MacDonald, Wimer and Kirtley. The Hartville garrison taken on January 9 is given by Britton as thirty-five militia and by Marmaduke as some 50. The expedition total and the No. 9 return are recorded under Springfield and not assigned here.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The frozen CS 329 has no inspected basis.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, volume I (Putnam's, second edition, revised, 1891) is a retrospective history whose title page says it is based upon the official reports of named Federal and Confederate commanders; its preface says the author served with the Federal army in that section and almost invariably took the official reports as a guide for numbers and casualties. It is not independent of the Official Records families and is treated as partly a participant's interested Union account. Marmaduke's January 18 and February 1, 1863 reports are one author family of interested Confederate accounts; Holmes's printed indorsement and the compiled No. 9 casualty return (garbled in OCR) are not counted as further families. Official Records Series I, Volume XXII, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
